description: baseline

Build a tensor-core batched Jacobi eigensolver that routes the O(n^3) interior onto B200 tensor cores the baseline never touches (it is 100% CUDA-core GEMV+sytrd). Use the symmetric two-sided/block-Jacobi formulation on A (orthogonal similarity J^T A J), or one-sided on A with explicit sign recovery, applying rotations as batched GEMM via torch.bmm (BF16/TF32) and/or Triton tl.dot; iterate to a HOST-VISIBLE off-diagonal-norm tolerance (not a fixed sweep count) so clustered/repeated/mixed benchmark cases still converge. Finish with an FP32 orthonormalization (CholeskyQR2 or Newton-Schulz) of Q and FP32 Rayleigh-quotient L=diag(Q^T A Q), sorted ascending with Q permuted to match.

Tensor-core block Jacobi first cut: round-robin block-pair eigh + diagonal-order matching (fixes Jacobi stall) + bmm rotation application + FP32 CholeskyQR2/Rayleigh finish. All 12 bench cases pass at small batch; at full B=640 the 2 mixed shapes miss eigen gate (scaled 211/215 vs 200). Runtime dominated by subproblem eigh (slow). Needs more convergence + magnitude prescaling for test cases.

Complete converging tensor-core block-Jacobi: passes ALL 39 test + 13 benchmark shapes. Geomean 589517us vs baseline 56255us (~10.5x SLOWER). Key correctness fixes: diagonal-order matching of sub-block eigenvectors (makes Jacobi converge at all; sorted placement stalls off-diag at 0.66), power-of-two prescale for extreme-magnitude LAPACK test cases, FP32-forced CholeskyQR2 finish (TF32 floors ortho at 7e-3), cuSOLVER per-matrix safety net for pathological mixed-batch matrices. nsys: subproblem cuSOLVER eigh (sytrd4_cta+laed*) is >50% of time; my TF32 tensor-core bmm application is only ~3%. Block Jacobi is structurally subproblem-bound and uncompetitive here.

Built a complete, correct, validated tensor-core block-Jacobi eigensolver (commit 98fe6b9d4): passes ALL 39 test + 13 benchmark shapes, geomean 589517us vs baseline 56255us = ~10.5x SLOWER. KEY INSIGHT (worth reusing): diagonal-order matching of sub-block eigenvectors -- assign eigenvector k to the axis whose original diagonal entry has rank k -- is what makes block Jacobi converge AT ALL; naive sorted eigh placement permutes the diagonal each round, creating a limit cycle that stalls the off-diagonal at ~0.66 of initial mass (this is non-obvious and cost me 4 diagnostic iterations). Also needed: power-of-two prescale for extreme-magnitude LAPACK test cases, FP32-forced CholeskyQR2 finish (TF32 floors orthogonality at 7e-3, fails the tight max-over-batch ORTH gate), cuSOLVER per-matrix safety net for pathological mixed-batch matrices that still stall. HARD NEGATIVE RESULT with numbers: block Jacobi cannot beat baseline here. nsys confirms subproblem cuSOLVER eigh (sytrd4_cta+laed*, >50%) dominates; my TF32 tensor-core bmm application is ~3%. I measured every subproblem option: cuSOLVER eigh on 2560x128 = 28ms/round; naive in-SMEM custom CUDA Jacobi kernel = 333ms/round (WORSE); fast batched-Jacobi path at m<=16 = 2.24ms but needs 63 rounds. Decisive: the bmm APPLICATION ALONE (TF32, 56 rounds, free subproblem) is 139ms for n=512 B=640 vs baseline 170ms -- so even a perfect/free subproblem solver yields at most ~1.2x on the dominant shape, and Jacobi does O(sweeps*n^3) work vs cuSOLVER's O(n^3). RECOMMEND: do not pursue Jacobi further for speed. The frontier (#1 az 33954us, 1.66x) is reached by a different angle -- likely better cuSOLVER batching, reduced-precision direct methods, or structured fast-paths (#4 is triton_diagonal). Point next briefs at: (a) genuinely-batched GEMM-heavy spectral divide & conquer / QDWH-eig polar decomposition (more GEMM-bound, fewer passes than Jacobi), or (b) speeding the launch-bound small shapes (n=32/176/352 carry 3/13 of geomean).

Your dead-end findings localized the entire remaining geomean to the dense n=512/1024 GEMV-bound sytrd interior, and named the one lever cuSOLVER's batched API cannot express: a reduced-precision two-stage solve with FP32 refinement. Stage A: get APPROXIMATE eigenpairs cheaply on tensor cores - a low-precision (BF16/TF32) tridiagonalization or a coarse approximate diagonalization, fast and sloppy. Stage B: REFINE to pass the gates entirely with batched GEMM (tensor-core), exploiting the loose ~1-2 digit tolerance - e.g. Rayleigh-Ritz: form the small projected matrix M=Q^T A Q (batched bmm), diagonalize the SMALL M, update Q<-Q@eigvecs(M); and/or a couple of subspace-iteration / Newton refinement steps. The point: replace cuSOLVER's expensive FP32 BLAS-2 sytrd with cheap tensor-core GEMM passes that the loose tolerance makes sufficient. Finish with FP32 CholeskyQR2/Newton-Schulz reortho of Q and FP32 Rayleigh-quotient L=diag(Q^T A Q), L ascending with Q permuted to match. Two-stage reduced-precision solve built+benchmarked: Stage A TF32 block-Jacobi coarse diag + Stage B FP32 CholeskyQR2/Rayleigh + cuSOLVER fallback. Passes all 39 test + 13 bench; geomean 588223us vs baseline 56255us (~10.5x SLOWER). Measured-not-reasoned negatives: (a) cuSOLVER eigh on nearly-diagonal M == dense (no near-diag exploit), (b) perturbative GEMM M-diagonalizer diverges on near-degenerate spectra, (c) 1-4 block-Jacobi sweeps + finish FAIL the gates (need ~16-20; subproblem eigh dominates), (d) tensor-core tridiag ceiling only ~1.35x since eigh(tridiagonal)=140 vs dense 191 (D&C is the dominant 74%, = W0 front), pure-torch blocked tridiag already 167ms >= cuSOLVER, (e) 1e-3 noise on TRUE eigenvectors already fails the eigen gate -- tighter than '1-2 digits'.

Brief-2 (reduced-precision two-stage) BUILT, BENCHMARKED, COMMITTED -- conclusively does NOT beat cuSOLVER. Final artifact (commit 37f6d864): Stage A TF32 block-Jacobi coarse diagonalization + Stage B FP32 CholeskyQR2/Rayleigh + cuSOLVER per-matrix safety net. Passes all 39 test + 13 bench shapes; geomean 588223us vs baseline 56255us (~10.5x SLOWER). Every negative below is MEASURED from a built kernel, not reasoned: (1) Rayleigh-Ritz cannot win because cuSOLVER eigh on a NEARLY-DIAGONAL M costs the same 25ms as on dense A -- cuSOLVER does not exploit near-diagonality, so the RR refine step is as expensive as a full solve. (2) No cheap GEMM-only M-diagonalizer exists for the benchmark spectra: first-order perturbation theory (U=I+X, X_ij=M_ij/(d_j-d_i)) DIVERGES on near-degenerate eigenvalues, which the clustered/repeated/mixed shapes have. (3) Few-sweep block-Jacobi Stage A (1-4 sweeps) + FP32 finish FAILS the gates even at the loose tolerance; ~16-20 sweeps are needed and the per-sweep small-block eigh sub-problem dominates (15ms/round x 7 rounds x 16 sweeps). (4) The tensor-core-tridiagonalization lever has a hard ceiling of only ~1.35x: eigh on a TRIDIAGONAL matrix is 140ms vs 190ms dense (the sytrd tridiagonalization is only ~26% of the cost), and the divide&conquer (laed*) is the dominant ~74% -- and the D&C is worker-0's spectral-D&C front, not mine. A pure-PyTorch blocked tridiagonalization is already 167ms (>= cuSOLVER's complete 191ms eigh) because the panel BLAS-2 (the per-column A@v matvecs) dominates and torch can't beat cuSOLVER's fused version. (5) IMPORTANT surprising gate fact: adding just 1e-3 noise to TRUE eigenvectors already FAILS the eigen-equation gate (the residual is weighted by eigenvalue spread), so Stage A must produce >2-digit-accurate eigenvectors -- TIGHTER than the brief's '1-2 digit tolerance' assumption, which is the root reason no cheap/sloppy Stage A suffices. NEW REGIME DISCOVERY for the manager: cuSOLVER batched eigh has a sharp regime change near n~128 -- eigh at n=128 B=640 is 4.2ms but n=256 is 47ms (11x for 2x size), n=512 is 191ms. If the n=512/1024 problem could be expressed as independent n<=128 subproblems it would be ~10x faster, but the only ways to do that (spectral D&C merge = W0, or band reduction = W2) are the other workers' fronts. CONCLUSION across my 3 briefs: the dense n=512/1024 D&C interior is the entire remaining geomean and it is firmly W0/W2 territory; my distinct angles (Jacobi, rank-structure, small-shape, reduced-precision-tridiag+RR) are all measured dead ends.
